# Performance and Bundle Impact

Covers Dimension 8: Runtime overhead of generated clients, bundle sizes,
and tree-shaking behavior.

See [citations.md](../citations.md) for full source details.

## Bundle Size Comparison

| Library | Size | Source |
|---------|------|--------|
| openapi-fetch | 6 KB (minified) | [1] |
| openapi-react-query | 1 KB | [2] |
| axios | 32 KB | [1] |
| superagent | 55 KB | [1] |
| Native fetch | 0 KB (platform built-in) | — |

openapi-fetch is 5.3x smaller than axios and 9.2x smaller than superagent. [1]

Note: openapi-fetch sizes are self-reported by the project documentation.
axios and superagent sizes are cited by openapi-fetch docs for comparison, not
independently verified.

## Runtime Performance

openapi-fetch reports 300k ops/s for GET requests. [1]

No benchmark methodology details (hardware, concurrency, comparison baselines)
were provided. The number is self-reported. [1]

The library is described as having "virtually zero runtime" — type checking
happens entirely at build time. Methods (GET, PUT, POST) are thin wrappers
around native Fetch API. [1]

## Tree-Shaking Behavior

### Function-Based (Tree-Shakeable)

hey-api defaults to flat/function-based SDK generation (`operations.strategy:
'flat'`), producing individually exported functions [4]:

```typescript
export const addPet = (options: Options<AddPetData>) => { /* ... */ };
```

These are tree-shakeable — bundlers can eliminate unused functions. [4]

### Class-Based (NOT Tree-Shakeable)

hey-api class-based SDKs (`operations.strategy: 'single'`) produce an
instantiable class. These do NOT support tree-shaking. [4]

The hey-api migration from openapi-typescript-codegen changed the default from
class-based to function-based, specifically for tree-shaking. [5]

### Type-Only Generation (Zero Runtime Cost)

openapi-typescript generates `.d.ts` type declarations that are completely
erased at build time — zero impact on the production bundle. The runtime cost
is only openapi-fetch (6 KB). [1]

This contrasts with full codegen tools (orval, hey-api, swagger-typescript-api)
where generated service functions become part of the runtime bundle.

## Path-Based Client Performance

The `createPathBasedClient` variant of openapi-fetch "has performance
implications" but specifics are not documented. [1]

It also does NOT support middleware attachment. [1]

## HTTP Client Size Trade-offs

orval v8 supports both Fetch and Axios as HTTP backends. [6] Using the native
Fetch client avoids the axios dependency (32 KB). [1]

## Architecture Impact on Bundle

| Architecture | Runtime Bundle Impact |
|-------------|---------------------|
| Type-only (openapi-typescript + openapi-fetch) | 6 KB wrapper only |
| Full codegen, function-based (hey-api flat) | Generated functions + HTTP client |
| Full codegen, class-based (hey-api single) | All generated code (no tree-shaking) |
| Full codegen + validation (Zod) | Generated code + Zod runtime (~14 KB) |

The total stack cost for the openapi-typescript ecosystem: openapi-fetch (6 KB)
+ openapi-react-query (1 KB) = 7 KB total. [1][2] This excludes @tanstack/
react-query itself, which is a peer dependency.
